chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ibn Mahbub from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a tooth is struck, it is waited upon for a year; if it falls out, the striker is fined five hundred dirhams; and if it does not fall out but turns black, he is fined two-thirds of its blood money (diya).
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for breaking a tooth in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar details the specific financial compensation (diya) for dental injury, distinguishing between the complete loss of a tooth (500 dirhams) and its damage without falling out (two-thirds of its value). It reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach to quantifying bodily harm, emphasizing the preservation of the tooth's integrity and the economic valuation of dental health in cases of assault.
